verses.1: Agrippa then said to Paul, “You may speak on my behalf.” At that, Paul stretched out his hand to refuse.
verses.2: Regarding everything that I accuse the Jews of doing, King Agrippa, I am willing to defend myself against your accusations today.
verses.3: I am especially well-versed in all the matters related to Judaism. Therefore, I hope to hear your long-winded explanations patiently.
verses.4: So, those who live in my community since their youth, all the Jews living in Jerusalem, regard them as being part of our own people.
verses.5: Let those who are above me testify, if they wish, that according to the strict rules of our religion, I was a Pharisee.
verses.6: And now, in hope for the message that has been given to our fathers by God, I stand here to make a judgment.
verses.7: He hopes that the twelve-horned one will be worshipped by us, day and night. For whom I place this hope is known only to the Jews, my king.
verses.8: How unjust it is for you to judge whether God resurrects the dead.
verses.9: I therefore decided that I must do many things against the name of Jesus Nazarite.
verses.10: And I also did what I could in Jerusalem. I put many of the saints in prison. I took away the authority that belonged to the high priests. I punished them and destroyed them.
verses.11: And by punishing them repeatedly for all their offenses, I forced them to suffer greatly. I also made it impossible for them to enter or stay in the surrounding towns.
verses.12: While traveling to Damascus, he was accompanied by the authority and permission of the high priests.
verses.13: We saw days of equal length along the road, oh king. From above, the brightness of the sun illuminated them, and it also illuminated those who were with me.
verses.14: In all those times when we were thrown onto the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in Hebrew: “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” It was a harsh and cruel voice.
verses.15: I said, “Who are you, sir?” The man replied, “I am Jesus, whom you are seeking.”
verses.16: But rise up and stand on your feet. For this very purpose have I come to you. You will serve me as a witness of what you saw and heard from me.
verses.17: Distinguished among the people and among the nations, to those whom I send you as my representatives.
verses.18: To close their eyes, so that they may return from darkness to light, and for Satan’s power to be taken away from them. To be freed from their sins, and to have faith in Me alone.
verses.19: Therefore, King Agrippa, I did not become a threat to the heavens’ vision.
verses.20: But to those in Damascus, as well as to Jerusalem and all of Judea, I encourage them to repent and return to God. They deserve to be rewarded for their repentance.
verses.21: For this reason, the Jews tried to take control of the temple.
verses.22: Therefore, I testified as a witness to everything that happened from the time of God until this day, both for those who were small and for those who were great. I said nothing that was contrary to what the prophets said about what would happen in the future, including Moses’ words.
verses.23: If Christ was a victim, if he was the first to bring light to the resurrection of the dead, for both the people and the nations.
verses.24: When he heard this, Phestos said loudly, “Mai, my lord! You have written so many things in letters that they seem like madness.”
verses.25: And Paulus said: “I do not believe, I say, that you are right or wise. Instead, I believe in words that are true and sensible.”
verses.26: For the king will surely question these matters. I will speak to him in such a way that he won’t be convinced by my words. After all, it’s not something that can be done without proper consideration.
verses.27: Do you believe, King Agrippa, in the prophets? I know that you do believe.
verses.28: And Agrippa to Paul: In a little while, you will be able to convince someone to become a Christian.
verses.29: And Paul said: “Euxaimein, not only to me, but also to all those who listen to me today, will happen such things. And I am free from these bonds.”
verses.30: The king and the governor also Anesstes, along with Bernike and those who were with them.
verses.31: And as they moved away from each other, they said to one another, “This man deserves no death or punishment.”
verses.32: But Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could not be called a king, unless he were invited by Caesar himself.”
